endorsements.quote: The CAID should lead the AI innovation in healthcare, serving as a collaborative hub where stakeholders converge to identify problems, define strategies, assess infrastructure and feasibility, recognize limitations, develop algorithms, and evaluate the use and performance of AI as CDSS.
To sustain the relevance and accuracy of these systems, an ongoing process of audits and performance supervision is indispensable.

In such scenario, audits should evaluate the performance of the AI-based algorithms in population subgroups by different metrics and lead to an appropriate calibration and discrimination of the models.
An AI’s applicability, its outputs, and its developmental steps should be disclosed in a standardized datasheet.
Human-centered : AI should not replace, but rather augment human decision-making.

unlisted_practices: Use ETL pipelines to harmonize and integrate data from disparate sources rather than relying on broad data standardization.
Preserve uncertainty in AI output by providing information about the accuracy and precision of estimates.
Develop AI to address predefined healthcare needs rather than developing algorithms first and seeking applications later.
Design AI to adapt to individual patients and users rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach.
Build a digital culture among medical stakeholders to critically engage with AI-based decision support.
Use explainable AI so model decisions are interpretable to clinicians.
Adapt algorithmic stewardship locally to each institution's maturity in data quality, technological infrastructure, and digital culture.

screen.reason: This is a letter/commentary discussing the ethical principles (algor-ethics, human-in-the-loop, algorithmic stewardship, Clinical AI Departments) required for deploying AI in critical care.
